speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I need to clarify the onset and nature of this swelling. When did you first notice the pain in your right ring finger, and was there any specific injury or insect bite associated with it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant traumatic event. Did the swelling spread to the entire finger or just the distal tip, and is the skin over the area red or shiny?

REQUEST TEST: Plain_Ray_Xray_Fingers_Right

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that Pyelonephritis is an infection of the kidney and does not cause localized finger swelling; please ignore that previous advice. While we await your X-ray results, can you describe if the pain is throbbing or constant, and does the finger feel warm to the touch?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Doctor: That previous diagnosis of Pyelonephritis is incorrect for a finger injury; let's focus on the local symptoms. Does the pain feel throbbing or constant, and is the finger noticeably warm to the touch?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Fingers_Right

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the Right Hand: Preliminary findings indicate integrity of tendons; no evidence of tendon rupture or significant joint effusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is reassuring news regarding the tendons. Can you tell me if you have a visible puncture wound, a splinter, or any other foreign object embedded in the finger since the injury? Also, did you receive any antibiotics or take the pain medication prescribed by the previous doctor?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Fingers_Right

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of the Right Hand: No visible puncture wounds, splinters, or foreign objects embedded in the tissue. No significant fluid collection or abscess formation detected around the distal interphalangeal joint.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Tenosynovitis (early) or localized hematoma with soft tissue contusion. Given the trauma history and lack of abscess or tendon rupture on imaging, this is likely a deep soft tissue injury or early inflammatory response rather than infection.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
